Clean a NANP phone number down to its ten digits, or say why it is not one.

Adapted from Exercism's [problem specification](https://github.com/exercism/problem-specifications/tree/main/exercises/phone-number) (MIT). Listed under [Parsing & Validation](/examples/?subject=parsing-and-validation).

```nomi-run
// FILE: phone_number.nomi
//# Cleans up a North American phone number written by a user.

/// Why a phrase is not a NANP phone number.
pub enum Error {
    Letters
    Punctuation
    TooFewDigits
    TooManyDigits
    CountryCodeNotOne
    AreaCodeStartsWithZero
    AreaCodeStartsWithOne
    ExchangeCodeStartsWithZero
    ExchangeCodeStartsWithOne
}

/// Cleans a NANP phone number down to its ten digits, dropping punctuation
/// and a leading country code of 1.
pub fn clean(phrase: String) -> Result<String, Error> {
    codepoints = String.to_codepoints(phrase)

    if Iter.any(codepoints, Codepoint.is_letter) { return Err(.Letters) }

    if !Iter.all(codepoints, fn cp -> Codepoint.is_digit(cp) or is_separator(cp)) {
        return Err(.Punctuation)
    }

    digits = codepoints |> Iter.map(Codepoint.to_digit) |> Maybe.values()

    digits = national(digits)?

    case digits {
        [0, .._] -> Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithZero)
        [1, .._] -> Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithOne)
        [_, _, _, 0, .._] -> Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithZero)
        [_, _, _, 1, .._] -> Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithOne)
        _ -> digits |> Iter.map(Int.to_string) |> String.join() |> Ok()
    }
}

/// Strips the country code from eleven digits, so ten remain.
fn national(digits: List<Int>) -> Result<List<Int>, Error> {
    count = Iter.count(digits)

    case digits {
        _ when count < 10 -> Err(.TooFewDigits)
        _ when count == 10 -> Ok(digits)
        [1, ..rest] when count == 11 -> Ok(rest)
        _ when count == 11 -> Err(.CountryCodeNotOne)
        _ -> Err(.TooManyDigits)
    }
}

fn is_separator(cp: Codepoint) -> Bool {
    case cp {
        ' ' or '(' or ')' or '-' or '.' or '+' -> True
        _ -> False
    }
}

// FILE: phone_number_test.nomi
import {
    phone_number
    phone_number.Error
}

test "cleans phone numbers" {
    cases = [
        #("cleans the number", "(223) 456-7890", Ok("2234567890")),
        #("cleans numbers with dots", "223.456.7890", Ok("2234567890")),
        #("cleans numbers with multiple spaces", "223 456   7890   ", Ok("2234567890")),
        #("invalid when 9 digits", "123456789", Err(Error.TooFewDigits)),
        #("invalid when 11 digits does not start with a 1", "22234567890", Err(.CountryCodeNotOne)),
        #("valid when 11 digits and starting with 1", "12234567890", Ok("2234567890")),
        #(
            "valid when 11 digits and starting with 1 even with punctuation",
            "+1 (223) 456-7890",
            Ok("2234567890"),
        ),
        #("invalid when more than 11 digits", "321234567890", Err(.TooManyDigits)),
        #("invalid with letters", "523-abc-7890", Err(.Letters)),
        #("invalid with punctuations", "523-@:!-7890", Err(.Punctuation)),
        #("invalid if area code starts with 0", "(023) 456-7890", Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithZero)),
        #("invalid if area code starts with 1", "(123) 456-7890", Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithOne)),
        #(
            "invalid if exchange code starts with 0",
            "(223) 056-7890",
            Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithZero),
        ),
        #(
            "invalid if exchange code starts with 1",
            "(223) 156-7890",
            Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithOne),
        ),
        #(
            "invalid if area code starts with 0 on valid 11-digit number",
            "1 (023) 456-7890",
            Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithZero),
        ),
        #(
            "invalid if area code starts with 1 on valid 11-digit number",
            "1 (123) 456-7890",
            Err(.AreaCodeStartsWithOne),
        ),
        #(
            "invalid if exchange code starts with 0 on valid 11-digit number",
            "1 (223) 056-7890",
            Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithZero),
        ),
        #(
            "invalid if exchange code starts with 1 on valid 11-digit number",
            "1 (223) 156-7890",
            Err(.ExchangeCodeStartsWithOne),
        ),
    ]

    subtests cases, #(description, phrase, expected), description {
        assert phone_number.clean(phrase) == expected
    }
}
```

## How it's written

- Errors are an `Error` enum, one variant per canonical error message; tests compare against variants, not message text.
- The checks run in the order the canonical errors imply: letters, then punctuation, then digit count, then the area and exchange codes.
- Digits become a `List<Int>`, so the area and exchange rules are list patterns (`[_, _, _, 0, .._]`) rather than string slicing.
- `national` uses a `case` with `when` guards on the count, so the eleven-digit `[1, ..rest]` pattern can sit among them.
- The work is per codepoint: `Codepoint.is_letter` finds letters, `Codepoint.is_digit` and `is_separator` find punctuation, and `Codepoint.to_digit` with `Maybe.values` keeps the digits as `Int`s in one stage. `is_letter` is Unicode, so `é` is a letter here, not punctuation; `is_digit` is ASCII only, so a full-width `１` is punctuation.
- `is_separator` is one `or` pattern of the six separators and a `_` arm.
